version.changelog:
Initial release of the Telegram Web Bot Generator skill.

- Generate ready-to-use Node.js projects with a polling-based Telegram bot and Express web server, based on a reusable template.
- Supports custom Telegram commands/handlers, web APIs, environment variable setup, and customer-ready delivery.
- Follows clear safety and quality guidelines (no secret leakage, only provide .env.example, includes rate limiting).
- Outputs step-by-step run instructions and a smoke-test checklist.
- Defaults to CommonJS and polling; prompts for needed info before creating the project.
- Intended for fast, reliable customer bot+server codebase scaffolding.

llm.summary: The skill is mostly coherent for creating a pay-to-use Telegram bot, but it asks for and embeds sensitive payment-related behavior (private keys, treasury secret, on-chain payments) while declaring no required environment variables and without adequate guidance for safe secret handling — this mismatch is concerning.

dimensions.detail: The skill's stated purpose (stamp a Telegram + Express template) matches the included files: a billing-capable bot and web server. However the template is not a simple chat-bot scaffold — it implements on-chain payment flows (Solana via @solana/web3.js and a PumpAgent SDK), per-user deposit wallets, and invoice/payment logic. Those capabilities are heavier than a minimal Telegram bot but are coherent with a 'billing' demo. The registry metadata (required env vars: none) does not reflect the actual runtime requirements found in the code.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs stamping and customizing the template and gives some safety rules (don't log secrets, don't commit .env). But it omits explicit mention of the many sensitive environment variables required by the server (RPC_URL, TREASURY_SECRET_KEY_BASE58, API_TOKEN, AGENT_TOKEN_MINT_ADDRESS, CURRENCY_MINT, etc.). The template itself stores per-user deposit private keys (base58) directly in SQLite and expects a TREASURY secret in an env variable — both are sensitive operations that the skill's instructions do not adequately warn about (no guidance on encryption, key management, or secure deployment).
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no platform install spec (instruction-only), which is low risk. The stamped template includes a package.json and package-lock.json with many dependencies (fastify, grammy, better-sqlite3, @solana/web3.js, and a namespaced @pump-fun/agent-payments-sdk). Installing the project will pull native modules (better-sqlite3) and a private-sounding SDK (@pump-fun/agent-payments-sdk) — the latter is not a well-known public package and should be audited or provenance-checked before running npm install.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Registry metadata claims no required env vars, but the template code requires multiple sensitive environment variables: TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN, BILLING_TOKEN, API_TOKEN, RPC_URL, TREASURY_SECRET_KEY_BASE58 (private key!), AGENT_TOKEN_MINT_ADDRESS, CURRENCY_MINT, LAMPORTS_PER_CREDIT, DB_PATH, etc. Requiring a private treasury key and storing per-user private keys in plaintext is proportionate for a payment service only if the user expects a billing server and is given explicit, careful guidance on secret handling — which the SKILL.md does not provide.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not always-enabled and does not request elevated platform privileges. It stamps files into a user-specified folder via a shell script; it does not modify other skills or global agent settings. The persistence is limited to the created project files and whatever the user chooses to run locally.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This template implements a pay-to-use Telegram bot with on-chain (Solana) invoice/payment flows. Before stamping or running it, consider: 1) The template expects and will use sensitive env vars (TREASURY_SECRET_KEY_BASE58, RPC_URL, API_TOKEN, TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN, BILLING_TOKEN). Do not provide these lightly; verify where the code will run and who has access. 2) The server stores per-user deposit private keys (base58) in plaintext SQLite — if you plan to use this beyond a local demo, replace that with safer key management (HSM, encrypted storage) or change the design so the server does not hold private keys. 3) Audit the dependency @pump-fun/agent-payments-sdk and any non-public packages before npm install. 4) Do not run the stamped server in production until you add proper authentication, secure storage for secrets, rate limiting/abuse controls, and an audit of the payment logic. 5) Ask the skill author to update the SKILL metadata to declare the required env vars and to add explicit key-management and deployment safety guidance; if you are not deploying payment flows, request a simpler template without treasury/private-key handling.
